claims.text: Dynamic mechanical behavior in solidified equiatomic Co-free FeNiCrMn is governed by a switch between dislocation glide and deformation twinning.
Dislocation glide dominates in FeNiCrMn at higher temperatures and lower strain rates.
Deformation twinning dominates in FeNiCrMn at lower temperatures and higher strain rates.
The proposed deformation-mode switch is mediated by stacking-fault energy that is sensitive to temperature and strain rate.
The tested material is fully solidified, equiatomic Co-free FeNiCrMn with a homogeneous microstructure and minimal pre-existing defects.
Deformation twins become activated and increase in density when stacking-fault energy is sufficiently reduced.
Low temperature and high strain rate reduce the effective stacking-fault energy of FeNiCrMn.
Reduced effective stacking-fault energy promotes deformation-twin nucleation in FeNiCrMn.
Deformation twinning provides an alternative deformation pathway that enhances the strength-ductility balance.
Low-temperature, high-strain-rate deformation will produce a significant increase in twin-boundary density.
Increased twin-boundary density will correlate with enhanced work-hardening rate and strength.
High-temperature, low-strain-rate deformation will be characterized primarily by dislocation motion with minimal twinning.
In equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi under similar conditions, Co supports more consistent dislocation glide and less pronounced twinning.
The hypothesis is restricted to homogeneous, fully solidified FeNiCrMn without significant microstructural heterogeneity or large pre-existing defect populations.
Residual stresses and compositional fluctuations are outside the proposed hypothesis.
Local chemical ordering could influence the deformation mechanism in FeNiCrMn.
